newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Southeast Asian airlines cancel Cambodia flights.
newsitem.headline: Southeast Asian airlines cancel Cambodia flights.

text.p: Several Southeast Asian airlines on Sunday suspended flights to Phnom Penh after renewed fighting in the Cambodian capital between force loyal to the country's two prime ministers.
Malaysia Airlines said in a statement on Sunday that it was suspending its flights to and from Phnom Penh "with immediate effect until further notice".
MAS flies to the Cambodian city on Sundays, Mondays, Wednesdays and Fridays.
The Malaysian flagship carrier said that its flights from Vientiane via Phnom Penh were also suspended "due to logistic reason". It did not elaborate.
In Hanoi, a passenger services official with Vietnam Airlines said the airline had suspended indefinitely all flights to Cambodia.
"Today all the flights are cancelled because there is a war there," the official in Ho Chi Minh City said. "We don't know exactly when they will start again."
He said Vietnam's flag carrier had flown to Phnom Penh from Ho Chi Minh City on Saturday afternoon, but the plane was unable to return because Phnom Penh airport had been closed.
Vietnam Airlines flies between Ho Chi Minh City and Phnom Penh twice a day and Cambodia's Royal Air Cambodge has one scheduled flight a day on the same route.

On Sunday morning, Singapore's SilkAir recorded announcement of information on delayed flights said: "In view of Phnom Penh's political instability, please note (the) Cambodian airport is closed", adding that SilkAir's daily flight had been cancelled. It gave no information on Monday's flight.
Royal Air Cambodge had also cancelled its Sunday flight due to airport closure but had made no decision yet on Monday's flight.
